name: @vkruglikov/telegram-mcp

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Show which Telegram account this server is signed in as.

tools.name: list_chats
tools.description: List recent dialogs, newest first. Use the returned chat_id for every other tool.

tools.name: search_chats
tools.description: Find dialogs by title or username. Matches across scripts, so "Вадим" finds "Vadim" and "Sasha" finds "Саша". Several chats often match a common first name — check the results and pick the right chat_id before sending anything.

tools.name: search_public_chats
tools.description: Search all of Telegram — not the user's own dialogs — for public channels, groups, bots and users by name or @username. Use this to find a chat the user has never opened; use search_chats for the ones they already have. Results are split into "mine" (their own contacts and dialogs) and "public" (everyone else). Public results are strangers: several channels share one name, and the flags say which is verified and which is flagged as a scam.

query.description: Name, topic or @username. Telegram matches usernames by prefix.

tools.name: search_public_posts
tools.description: Full-text search over posts in every public channel on Telegram, whether or not the user follows them. This is the whole network, not the account: use search_messages for the user's own chats. Telegram rations these searches — the result reports how many free ones are left today, so do not spend them on repeated near-identical queries.

query.description: Keywords, or a #hashtag. Matches the text of public posts.

tools.name: get_history
tools.description: Read the most recent messages of a chat, newest first. Read-only: this does not mark anything as read.

chat.description: Chat identifier from list_chats or search_chats: a numeric chat_id, a @username, or "me" for Saved Messages. Do not invent one.

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Full-text search over messages, inside one chat or across the whole account when chat is omitted.

chat.description: Chat identifier from list_chats or search_chats: a numeric chat_id, a @username, or "me" for Saved Messages. Do not invent one.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a text message. It is delivered immediately and there is no undo — confirm the chat_id came from list_chats or search_chats first.

chat.description: Chat identifier from list_chats or search_chats: a numeric chat_id, a @username, or "me" for Saved Messages. Do not invent one.

tools.name: send_file
tools.description: Upload a local file to a chat. Delivered immediately, no undo.

chat.description: Chat identifier from list_chats or search_chats: a numeric chat_id, a @username, or "me" for Saved Messages. Do not invent one.

path.description: Absolute path to a local file

tools.name: download_media
tools.description: Download the media attached to one message. Returns the saved path.

chat.description: Chat identifier from list_chats or search_chats: a numeric chat_id, a @username, or "me" for Saved Messages. Do not invent one.

tools.name: mark_read
tools.description: Mark a chat as read. The other side sees read receipts — this is visible to them.

chat.description: Chat identifier from list_chats or search_chats: a numeric chat_id, a @username, or "me" for Saved Messages. Do not invent one.

tools.name: sample_my_messages
tools.description: Collect messages the user themselves wrote, as raw material for describing how they write. Private chats only, text only, no recipients — this is a style sample, not a transcript.

chats.description: How many recent private dialogs to draw from

min_length.description: Skip anything shorter — "ok", "+", a lone emoji

tools.name: save_style_profile
tools.description: Store the description of how the user writes. Replaces any previous one. It is loaded on every start and used when drafting on their behalf.

tools.name: get_style_profile
tools.description: Show the stored writing-style profile, if there is one.

instructions:
This server is signed in as the user's own Telegram account, not a bot.
Anything it sends comes from them personally.

Resolving a chat
- Never invent or guess a chat_id. Take it from list_chats or search_chats.
- One first name usually matches several dialogs. If more than one result is a
  plausible match, show them and ask which one — do not pick for the user.
- The user says a name the way they speak it; the contact may be saved in another
  script or spelling. search_chats already matches "Вадим" against "Vadim" and
  back, so search the name as given first.
- If that finds nothing, the contact is probably saved under something else: a
  short form (Саша for Александр, Dima for Dmitry), a surname, a @username, or a
  nickname. Try those, or fall back to list_chats and look. Report that you could
  not find them rather than sending to the closest guess.
- "me" is Saved Messages, the user's own notes.

Searching the rest of Telegram
- search_chats and search_messages only ever see the user's own dialogs.
  search_public_chats and search_public_posts see all of Telegram, including
  channels the user has never joined and people they have never met.
- A chat_id from a public result is a stranger. Reading its history is fine;
  writing to it is a first contact from the user's personal account, so say who
  it is and wait for a yes before sending anything.
- Names in the public directory are not unique — impostors copy popular channels
  outright. Prefer verified results, skip the ones flagged as scam, and show the
  username and member count when reporting a find.
- Free public post searches are metered per day. The result says how many are
  left; refine a query before repeating it, and do not sweep the same topic twice.

Before sending
- Messages and files are delivered immediately and cannot be unsent.
- Name the recipient back to the user before the first message of a conversation,
  so a wrong match is caught before it is delivered rather than after.

Reading
- get_history and search_messages do not mark anything as read. Only mark_read does,
  and the other side sees the read receipt, so do not call it just to tidy up.
- Chat 777000 ("Telegram") is the service chat. It contains login codes and account
  notifications. Do not read it unless asked, and never repeat a code from it.
